newsitem.title: GUYANA: CRICKET-JADEJA HITS CENTURY AS INDIA DOMINATE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JADEJA HITS CENTURY AS INDIA DOMINATE.

text.p: Opener Ajay Jadeja, who narrowly missed out on his maiden test century this week, hit 106 as India dominated the first day of their four day match against Guyana on Friday.
Backed by Saurav Ganguly who made 90 and acting captain Mohammad Azharrhuddin who made 59, Jadeja led the attack as India progressed to 294 for five at the close after choosing to bat.

Jadeja, run out for 96 in the rain-hit fourth test against the West Indies on Tuesday, attacked from the start of his innings and reached his half century in 107 minutes off 73 balls. He survived a chance on 47 when he was dropped at second slip off pacer Colin Stuart.
Jadeja eventually fell victim to paceman Reon King when he was bowled for 106, which he hit off 162 balls. His innings included 14 fours.
Jadeja shared a 143-run second wicket partnership with Ganguly after experienced opener Navjot Sidhu went for two in the seventh over, caught at backward point by Neil Mcgarrell off King.
Azharuddin, who has been struggling for form on the tour, was King's third victim, giving a return catch to the former West Indies youth pacer for 59, including eight fours.
Ganguly played a defiant innings, falling ten short of a century when Guyana captain Shivnarine Chanderpaul induced him to pull to deep backward square, where Andre Percival held a well-judged catch.

Chanderpaul claimed another victim with his next delivery when Vangipurappu Laxman, who only retained his place in the fourth test because Sidhu was unfit, was caught at first slip by Mahendra Nagamootoo for nought.
At the close Robin Singh was on 26 and wicket-keeper Syed Karim on one.
